Sequence Editor

Edit startup, shutdown, and afterburner transitions. Normal running controls are configured on Controllers.

Afterburner operation has two parts: choose the trigger source and wiring in Hardware - AB Trigger & Arming, then tune the trigger value, gate limits and light-up/light-off actions here. Ignition, flame-confirmation, and lit-running fuel behavior remain with the relevant output cards on Controllers.

Entry Conditions

Throttle Trigger (%) Throttle demand at which automatic afterburner entry becomes eligible.
AB Input Trigger (%) Works for ADC or servo-PWM AB input; signal type and GPIO stay in Hardware.
Minimum N1 (rpm) Minimum healthy core speed required before afterburner light-up is allowed.
Maximum N1 (rpm, 0 = off) Optional upper core-speed gate for light-up. Zero disables this entry gate.
Maximum EGT To Light (°C, 0 = off) Optional maximum turbine temperature for starting afterburner light-up. Zero disables this entry gate.

Fault behavior: If Light Up faults (ignition not confirmed), the afterburner fuel valve closes, its fuel pump stops, and the afterburner igniter turns off immediately. The main engine continues running normally. AB state resets - you can retry from the dashboard.
Light Up Sequence

Runs when the afterburner trigger is activated. Default: check readiness → open the AB fuel valve → start the AB fuel pump → ignite → confirm flame → stabilize. If empty, the built-in default sequence is used.

Light Off Sequence

Runs when the afterburner trigger is released. Default: stop the AB fuel pump → close the AB fuel valve → turn the AB igniter off.
